同.meaning: A photographer peers through a <part>frame</part> at a pair of twins. Draw <part>one</part> line across them: same eyebrows. Below it, a <part>mouth</part> each: same grin. You can't tell them apart: they're exactly the <kanji>same</kanji>.
同.on: They even bake bread from the very same lump of <sound>dough</sound>.
同.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' you laugh, as they both bite the same <sound>na</sound>an at once.

牙.meaning: A long curved tooth juts sideways out of a beast's jaw, with a hook at the root and a sharp slash at the tip. The beast tosses its head and the tooth flashes white in the sun. That's a <kanji>tusk</kanji>.
牙.on: A tiny <sound>ge</sound>cko clings to the tip of the tusk and enjoys the ride.
牙.kun: An elephant hangs its <sound>key</sound>s on its tusk, and a passing sheep bleats '<sound>Bah</sound>!'

邪.meaning: A villain sticks a sharp <part>tusk</part> on the end of his flagpole and flies a black <part>pennant</part> beneath it. He steals sweets from children and laughs as he marches by. Truly <kanji>wicked</kanji>.
邪.on: He hides all the stolen sweets in a big glass <sound>ja</sound>r.
邪.kun: He swaps your <sound>yo</sound>gurt for glue, hides a <sound>ko</sound>ala in your bed and paints your <sound>shee</sound>p green.

初.meaning: A young knight draws a <part>sword</part> and gives it a swing. Clang! It knocks the <part>weathervane</part> clean off the roof. Everyone gasps, then forgives him: it's his <kanji>first time</kanji>.
初.on: He buys a new weathervane at a little <sound>sho</sound>p down the lane.
初.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' laugh his friends, and they drive him home in a <sound>jee</sound>p.

老.meaning: Long ago he threw a javelin so far that it's still out there, a <part>stuck javelin</part> in the field. Now he sits beside it, slurping soup from a <part>spoon</part> and telling the story again. He's an <kanji>old man</kanji> now.
老.on: Every year he plants a red <sound>ro</sound>se beside the javelin.
老.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>, my knees,' he sighs, getting up from his chair a little slower each year.

末.meaning: A <part>tree</part> grows so tall that a <part>one</part>-plank sign is nailed across its very top: no further. A squirrel climbs up, reads it, looks at the sky and sits down. This is the <kanji>end</kanji> of the tree.
末.on: At the end of the day, <sound>Ma</sound>ma squirrel rides home on a <sound>tsu</sound>nami of falling leaves.
末.kun: She ends her day with <sound>su</sound>shi and a boiled <sound>e</sound>gg.

始.meaning: A <part>woman</part> climbs onto a <part>pedestal</part>, lifts a starter's pistol and fires. Bang! Hundreds of runners dash off down the road. She's the one who makes the race <kanji>begin</kanji>.
始.on: Instead of a flag, she waves a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld to start them off.
始.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' she laughs, as one runner yells '<sound>Gee</sound>, it's started!' and is still tying his shoes.
